page_title: Writing a Web Server from Scratch

sources.entry: C#: _Writing a Web Server from Scratch_

summary.title: Writing a Web Server from Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a lightweight C# web server on top of HttpListener, step by step, covering async connection handling, static file routing, error pages and redirects.
keywords: http verbs get post put delete
takeaways: Build a basic web server in C# using HttpListener with an async accept loop limited by a semaphore.
Route requests by file extension to loader functions for images, HTML pages, and text files, setting proper content types.
Handle errors such as unknown types, missing pages and exceptions by redirecting to application-defined error pages.
Notice browser quirks such as favicon.ico requests and encoding warnings shown in the browser console.
summary.summary: The article walks through writing a small web server as a C# library (Listener, Router and SessionManager classes) with a console app hosting it, under 650 lines. It proceeds in steps: starting an HttpListener on localhost and local IPs, logging requests, serving files from a Website folder via an extension-to-loader map, then adding error enums, redirect-based error handling and try-catch exception handling. The author also gives an opinionated critique of MVC, ORM, attributes and IIS, and says verbs, authorization and sessions are next.
